title: In-Memory File System
statement:
Implement a tiny in-memory file system rooted at `/`.

Contract
- Construct an empty file system with `new Solution()`.
- `ls(path)` returns sorted child names for a directory, a singleton list containing the file name for a file, or an empty list for a missing path.
- `mkdir(path)` creates all missing directories along the path. Calling it for `/` is allowed and changes nothing.
- `addContentToFile(filePath, content)` creates the file and parent directories if needed, then appends `content`.
- `readContentFromFile(filePath)` returns the complete content of an existing file. Tests only read files that exist.

Examples
- After `mkdir /a/b` and `add /a/b/c.txt hi`, `ls /a/b` returns `[c.txt]`.
- Adding ` there` to `/a/b/c.txt` makes reading it return `hi there`.
hints: A directory node needs a map from names to child nodes.
Use a sorted map or sort directory names when listing.
While walking a path, create intermediate directory nodes only for operations that promise to create them.
inputSyntax: Input: operations separated by commas, for example: mkdir /a/b, add /a/b/c.txt hi, ls /a/b, read /a/b/c.txt
